section_1.title: The Core Problem: Contextual Ambiguity
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of language processing—words have different meanings depending on context. Establish the limitation of previous models that processed data sequentially (like reading one word at a time).
section_1.example: Comparing 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired' vs. '...because it was too wide.' (Explain how 'it' links to 'animal' vs. 'street').

section_2.title: The Intuition: The 'Spotlight' Analogy
section_2.content: Explain Attention as a 'weighted spotlight' that scans an entire sentence at once, assigning different importance (scores) to other words to better understand the current word.
section_2.example: Visualizing a library: When you look for a book, you don't read every shelf equally; you focus on relevant ones. A robot searching for 'Apple' focuses on keywords like 'fruit' or 'tech' while ignoring 'the' or 'a'.

section_3.title: The Mathematical Architecture: Q, K, and V
section_3.content: Break down Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V). Use a graphical analogy: Q is your search, K is the label on a folder, V is the content inside. The Score = Q × K^T, normalized by Softmax.
section_3.example: Animation: A visual 'matching' game where a 'Query' card searches a row of 'Key' cards to determine which 'Value' card is most relevant to retrieve.

section_4.title: The Mechanism in Motion: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
section_4.content: Explain the final calculation: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(dk))V. Focus on the visual aspect—how high scores make certain information 'brighter' for the next layer.
section_4.example: A heatmap visualization showing how the word 'bank' in 'The river bank' glows bright yellow when paired with 'river' but dim with 'money'.

section_5.title: Conclusion: From Attention to Intelligence
section_5.content: Summarize how stacking these attention layers allows models to capture complex relationships and long-range dependencies, powering LLMs like GPT.
section_5.example: Showing a final animation of a sentence transforming from raw text into a rich, interconnected web of relationships that the LLM 'understands'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

        lecture_lines = ["We calculate attention using Q, K, and V.", "Dot-product Q and K creates a heatmap.", "Softmax makes the focus sharper."]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism in Motion: Scaled Dot-Product Attention", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors for lecture lines
        c1, c2, c3 = "#FFD700", "#00FFFF", "#FF69B4"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(c1)
        q = Text("Q", color=c1).scale(1.2)
        k = Text("K", color=c2).scale(1.2)
